metadata.title: Oppn's Mock Parliament Debate: BJP's Sanju Verma Slams Rahul Gandhi Over Absenteeism In Parliament

window_analysis.main_issue: Criticism of the opposition's mock parliament and Rahul Gandhi's parliamentary attendance and engagement.
window_analysis.summary: BJP national spokesperson Sanju Verma and political analyst Rajat Sethi discuss the opposition's decision to hold a mock parliament. They criticize Rahul Gandhi and opposition leaders for absenteeism in Parliament, bypassing constitutional bodies like the Supreme Court, and opting for street protests instead of utilizing parliamentary procedures like Question Hour and Zero Hour.
discussion_points: The unprecedented nature of the opposition holding a mock parliament in the house of the leader of the opposition.
Allegations against Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders for being 'missing in action' (MIA) during crucial parliamentary debates and votes, such as the no-confidence motion.
Comparison of Rahul Gandhi's low parliamentary attendance average with the national average.
The opposition's shift from engaging in parliament or courts to holding protests and street demonstrations.
The availability of parliamentary mechanisms like Zero Hour for the opposition to raise issues without advance notice.

evidence.text: Sanju Verma, what we witnessed today was unprecedented.
Never before that in India or Indian political history has a mock parliament been held in the house of leader of opposition.
In August 2023, Gaurav Gogoi had moved a no-confidence motion against the Modi government.
Priyanka Padra was not there in the house.
Why is his average attendance in the last three Lok Sabha sessions 37% vis-a-vis all India averaged of 79.6%?
Why has Rahul Gandhi not utilised zero arc?
